chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Muyassar, who said:

I entered upon Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and he said: 'How are your companions?' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, we are considered worse in their eyes than the Jews, the Christians, the Magians, and those who associate partners [with God].' He (the narrator) said: 'He had been leaning [on a pillow], so he sat up straight, then said: 'How did you say?' I said, 'By Allah, we are considered worse in their eyes than the Jews, the Christians, the Magians, and those who associate [partners with God].'

He said: 'By Allah, no two of you will enter the Fire. No, by Allah, and not even one. By Allah, you are the ones about whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: “And they shall say: What is the matter with us that we do not see men whom we used to count among the evil? Was it that we (only) took them in scorn, or have our eyes (now) turned aside from them? That most surely is the truth: the contending one with another of the inmates of the fire.”'
Then he said: 'By Allah, they will be seeking you in the Fire, so they will not find even one of you therein.'

key_terms.تَخاصُمُ أَهْلِ النَّارِ: The contending of the inmates of the Fire
key_terms.لَا تَدْخُلُ النَّارَ مِنْكُمُ اثْنَانِ: No two of you will enter the Fire

ai.seo_question: Why does the Quran say we don't see the men we counted as evil in Paradise?
ai.summary: In this narrative from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) transforms the societal perception of the Shiites as 'evil' (*al-ashrar*) into a mark of honor, citing Quran 38:62-64 to reveal that those deemed wicked by the masses are actually the true believers destined for Paradise. The Imam emphatically assures Muyassar that not even one or two from among them will enter the Fire, illustrating the Shia concept of *al-gharba* (strangeness) where the faithful are often misunderstood or despised by the general public. This hadith underscores the theological principle that divine favor often aligns with those who remain steadfast in their distinct identity despite social ostracization.
